root_cause.text: The SMC TCP ULP implementation tried to “convert” an existing TCP socket into an SMC socket by in-place rewriting the associated `struct file`, dentry, and inode, breaking VFS lifetime/immutability invariants and enabling use-after-free conditions.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says the feature was “fundamentally broken” because it “attempts to convert an active TCP socket into an SMC socket by modifying the underlying `struct file`, dentry, and inode in-place,” which “violates core VFS invariants”; the patch removes `smc_ulp_init()`, where `smcsock->file = tcp->file;`, `smcsock->file->private_data = smcsock;`, `smcsock->file->f_inode = SOCK_INODE(smcsock);`, and `smcsock->file->f_path.dentry->d_inode = SOCK_INODE(smcsock);` were doing exactly that.

vuln_statements.content: smcsock->file->f_inode = SOCK_INODE(smcsock); /* replace inode when sock_close */

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify the SMC socket creation helper by dropping an unused argument and dead local variable.
intent_record.what: The static helper function was renamed from `__smc_create` to `smc_create`, its parameter list was reduced by removing the `struct socket *clcsock` argument, and the unused local declaration `struct smc_sock *smc;` was deleted from the function body.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the function interface so the creation routine no longer accepts a separate client socket pointer, which simplifies the call contract and removes an unused variable; the observable behavior of the remaining logic is unchanged in this hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate CLC socket creation into `smc_create_clcsk()` by removing inline conditional setup in `__smc_create()`.
intent_record.what: The code removed the explicit assignment of `smc = smc_sk(sk)` and the conditional logic that either stored an existing `clcsock` into `smc->clcsock` or called `smc_create_clcsk(net, sk, family)` only when `clcsock` was absent. It now unconditionally assigns `rc = smc_create_clcsk(net, sk, family);` after `sk` is created.
intent_record.how: At runtime, creation of the internal TCP socket for the CLC handshake/fallback is now always delegated to `smc_create_clcsk()`, instead of being partially handled inline and skipped when `clcsock` is already provided. This centralizes the setup path and changes ownership/initialization flow so the helper is responsible for the clcsock-related creation logic in all cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove SMC TCP ULP replacement support and related wrapper code to eliminate the affected socket transition path.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the local wrapper `smc_create()` and deletes the SMC TCP ULP support code: `smc_ulp_init()`, `smc_ulp_clone()`, and the `smc_ulp_ops` structure. The `smc_sock_family_ops` table still references `smc_create`, but that function is no longer defined in this hunk.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this eliminates the code path that allowed an established TCP socket to be replaced by an SMC socket via the TCP ULP mechanism, along with the associated clone-time ULP handling. As shown, it also removes the standalone family create wrapper, changing how SMC socket creation is wired in this file.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove TCP ULP registration from SMC initialization and simplify the failure unwind path after smc_inet_init().
intent_record.what: In smc_init(), the call to tcp_register_ulp(&smc_ulp_ops) and its associated error handling block were removed. The failure path after smc_inet_init() was also changed so that it now jumps to out_ib instead of out_ulp.
intent_record.how: At runtime, SMC initialization no longer explicitly registers the TCP ULP during this function, and any failure in smc_inet_init() now skips the removed ULP cleanup path and unwinds directly to the IB cleanup stage. This changes initialization and rollback sequencing for SMC setup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the TCP ULP unregister step from the `smc_init()` failure cleanup path.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the `out_ulp:` label and deletes the `tcp_unregister_ulp(&smc_ulp_ops);` cleanup call from the `smc_init()` error path, leaving `out_inet:` to fall through directly to `out_ib:`.
intent_record.how: On initialization failure after `smc_inet_exit()`, the code will no longer unregister the TCP ULP before continuing to the remaining cleanup path. This changes the teardown sequence for that failure case by skipping the ULP deregistration step.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the redundant TCP ULP unregister call from SMC module teardown.
intent_record.what: In `smc_exit()`, the call to `tcp_unregister_ulp(&smc_ulp_ops);` was removed, leaving the rest of the shutdown sequence unchanged.
intent_record.how: During module exit, SMC will no longer explicitly unregister its TCP ULP operations at this point, so the teardown path skips that unregister action while still disabling the static branch, exiting inet support, unregistering the socket family, and cleaning up core/IB state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the TCP ULP module alias for SMC so the module is no longer exposed or auto-loaded under the "smc" ULP name.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the `MODULE_ALIAS_TCP_ULP("smc")` line from the module metadata in the SMC socket family source file. The surrounding module author, description, license, and other aliases remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the module will no longer advertise itself as a TCP ULP named "smc". This prevents automatic module matching/loading through that alias path while leaving the rest of the module’s networking aliases intact.

consistency_review.core_intent: Remove redundant TCP ULP unregister handling from SMC teardown and related cleanup paths.

relevance_review.reason: The changes only remove an unused argument and a dead local variable in an SMC socket creation helper. They do not address or modify the problematic in-place rewriting of struct file/dentry/inode that caused the lifetime and use-after-free issue.

The change only refactors CLC socket creation logic into a helper and removes inline conditional setup. It does not address in-place rewriting of TCP socket file/dentry/inode structures or any VFS lifetime/immutability issue related to the UAF root cause.
The change directly removes the SMC TCP ULP socket replacement path that in-place rewrote the file/dentry/inode, which is the vulnerability root cause.

The changes remove TCP ULP registration from SMC initialization, which is directly tied to the flawed mechanism of converting a TCP socket into an SMC socket in place. That conversion path is the root cause of the VFS lifetime/immutability violation and resulting use-after-free risk, so this is a relevant fix.

The changes only remove redundant TCP ULP unregister cleanup in SMC teardown/init failure paths. They do not address the root cause involving in-place rewriting of struct file, dentry, and inode during TCP-to-SMC conversion, nor the resulting VFS lifetime/use-after-free issue.

The change only removes the SMC TCP ULP module alias and affects module exposure/auto-loading. It does not address the root cause of in-place rewriting of the file/dentry/inode during TCP-to-SMC conversion, nor the resulting VFS lifetime/use-after-free issue.

candidates.rationale: This is the core in-place socket conversion step: it transfers the existing TCP socket's file pointer to the new SMC socket, directly rewriting the VFS-backed file association and enabling lifetime/ownership corruption.
This mutates the existing file object to point at the new SMC socket, which is part of the unsafe rewrite of a live struct file and can break file/socket lifetime invariants.

candidates.content: smcsock->file->f_inode = SOCK_INODE(smcsock); /* replace inode when sock_close */
candidates.rationale: Directly overwriting the file's inode field is an in-place VFS object rewrite, matching the root cause of violating immutability/lifetime rules and risking use-after-free.
This changes the dentry's inode pointer for an existing open file, another direct violation of VFS invariants that can leave stale references and cause UAF.
Nulling out the original TCP socket's file after transplanting it to SMC is part of the unsafe ownership transfer that breaks the original file/socket relationship.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the fundamental in-place file transfer from the TCP socket to the SMC socket, which starts the unsafe conversion of one live socket into another and breaks VFS lifetime/ownership invariants.
This rewrites the live struct file to point at the new SMC socket, mutating an existing VFS object in place and contributing to the use-after-free-prone socket/file transplant.

vuln_statements.stmt_text: smcsock->file->f_inode = SOCK_INODE(smcsock); /* replace inode when sock_close */
vuln_statements.explanation: This directly overwrites the file's inode association, violating file immutability assumptions and matching the root cause of in-place VFS object rewriting.
This changes the dentry's inode pointer for an already-open file, another direct VFS lifetime/consistency violation that can leave stale references and trigger use-after-free.
This completes the unsafe ownership transfer by detaching the original TCP socket from its file after the transplant, breaking the original socket/file relationship.
